title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: MARLON'S DUCK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Marlon Tibbs, from Havre de Grace, Maryland.
For thirty-eight years, he pumped gas into boats at the town marina.
Then he retired, and learned the hardest job in the world is doing nothing.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE RECLINER
segments.quote: Painting's not important. The important thing is keeping busy.
segments.author: Grandma Moses
lines: By March, Marlon knew every crack in the ceiling.
His wife Denise pointed at a fridge magnet from Grandma Moses, who started painting in her seventies:
Painting's not important. The important thing is keeping busy.
Marlon had always wanted to carve a duck decoy.
So he bought a pocketknife and a block of cedar. That afternoon.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE LOAF
segments.quote: Nobody wants constructive criticism; it's all we can do to put up with constructive praise.
segments.author: Mignon McLaughlin
lines: Three weeks later, he showed his first duck to Miss Ida, an eighty-four-year-old carver.
She turned it over and said, Marlon, that's a lovely loaf of bread.
He sulked. Denise read him a line from the writer Mignon McLaughlin:
Nobody wants constructive criticism; it's all we can do to put up with constructive praise.
Next morning, he went back and asked Miss Ida what was wrong.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE BIRD
segments.quote: When the bird and the book disagree, always believe the bird.
segments.author: Birdwatcher's proverb
lines: Miss Ida tapped the library book under his arm and gave him an old birdwatcher's saying:
When the bird and the book disagree, always believe the bird.
So Marlon drove to the water at dawn with a thermos of coffee.
He watched real canvasback ducks ride the cold waves for hours.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: ONE DUCK
segments.quote: Try to learn something about everything and everything about something.
segments.author: Thomas Huxley
lines: In that library book, someone had copied a line from Thomas Huxley, the English scientist:
Try to learn something about everything and everything about something.
Marlon picked his something. The canvasback.
How it tucks its head in the wind. How it sits low and proud.
Denise said he knew more about one duck than about her.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE GARAGE
segments.quote: You can't use up creativity. The more you use, the more you have.
segments.author: Maya Angelou
lines: By summer, he'd carved twenty ducks, and feared he'd run out of ideas.
Then he found a bookmark with words from Maya Angelou:
You can't use up creativity. The more you use, the more you have.
So he carved one duck a night. Each looked a little more alive.
By winter, there was a duck in the bathtub.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FESTIVAL
segments.quote: Whatever you are, try to be a good one.
segments.author: William Makepeace Thackeray
lines: In May, he took second place for beginners at the spring decoy festival.
Then Jamal, the young guy who now pumps gas at his old dock, asked, Can you teach me?
Marlon said, I'm no master. Miss Ida quoted the novelist William Makepeace Thackeray:
Whatever you are, try to be a good one.
Now, every Saturday, two guys carve ducks in Marlon's garage.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Keep busy. Take the hard advice. Watch the bird. Go deep. Keep making. Pass it on.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Keep busy. Take the hard advice. Watch the real bird. Go deep. Keep making. Pass it on.
I tried carving a duck once. My wife called it a very brave potato.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
